name: Dingo
description: Dingo is a strategic card game for four players from Cleveland, Ohio. The game features a unique 'hunt' mechanic where diamonds (rabbits) are hunted in ascending order, with hearts (dingoes) and black cards (wolves) playing special roles. Players score points based on card values and hunt outcomes.

content.text: Dingo is a strategic card game for four players from Cleveland, Ohio. The game features a unique 'hunt' mechanic where diamonds (rabbits) are hunted in ascending order, with hearts (dingoes) and black cards (wolves) playing special roles. Players score points based on card values and hunt outcomes.

Country/Region of Origin: Cleveland, Ohio, USA
Time Period: Several years prior to 2017 documentation
Historical Development: Played in card game circles in Cleveland
Cultural Significance: Part of Cleveland's unique card game culture along with Democracy and Ribs

Minimum Players: 4
Maximum Players: 4
Optimal Players: 4
Partnerships: None - individual play

Type: Standard 52-card deck with special classifications
Number of Decks: 1
Jokers: Not included
Special classifications:
- Diamonds = 'rabbits' (Ace of diamonds = 'Ace rabbit')
- Hearts = 'dingoes'
- Spades and Clubs = 'wolves'

Standard 52-card deck
Table space for rabbit pile and discards
Score sheet

First dealer chosen randomly, passes left after each game
Dealer separates diamonds from deck (except Ace of diamonds stays in main pack)
Diamonds 2-K ordered low to high, placed face up in center (2 on top)
Main pack: 40 cards (13 hearts, 13 spades, 13 clubs, 1 Ace of diamonds)
Shuffle and deal 10 cards to each player

items.text: First to Five Games: Play a match where first player to win five games wins the match.
Running Total 100: Keep cumulative points across games; first to 100 points wins.
Conservative Ace Hunt: Table-specific ace-hunt play order and wolf timing conventions by prior agreement.
